statement: For a C1 associative composition law F on a connected capacity domain with right identity 1 and partial_2 F(a,1)=a for every a, F(a,b)=a*b.
proof_method: Differentiate associativity at the unit; IMR reduces the composition law to the ODE partial_b F(a,b)=F(a,b)/b; the unit fixes the integration constant.
cycle039_family_check: For F_k(a,b)=ab+k(a-1)(b-1), IMR holds for every nontrivial a iff k=0.

dimension_audit.exact_integer_associativity_triples: all triples a,b,c in 1..12 for k=0..5 are covered by unit tests
dimension_audit.higher_test: product reference marginal tested through a=100; nonzero k exclusion tested through k=19

novelty_boundary: Associative-function representation and invariant-differential methods are classical. Historical novelty is not claimed. PDT-specific novelty, if any, would have to lie in a future independent derivation or experiment establishing IMR from resource/distinction primitives.
limitations: IMR is not yet derived from PDT primitives.
The theorem fixes only a scalar effective-capacity law, not the full composite state/effect structure.
A differentiable continuous extension of effective capacity is assumed.
The result does not derive n=3 and does not produce a same-input deviation from quantum mechanics.
next_obligation: Derive or falsify IMR from the finite-resource PDT primitive; then test whether scalar multiplicativity plus resource constraints restricts full composite state/effect structures.
